background.text: Good. If you had to pick one single thing that happened this year that you feel was accomplished this year, what would it be?

background.speaker: [target]
background.text: I couldn't pick one single thing, and the reason why is because we've done so much in this close to 340 days or so. We've reorganized and restructured governance at the municipal building. We have implemented our act plan of being accountable, clear, and transparent. We've had a high focus on public safety. We've kept campaign promises from our campaigning about a citizen's review board. That's a campaign promise that was kept, as well as identifying funding through the federal justice department, as well as city dollars, to fully fund our body-worn cameras, our Knobbin machine, which is basically what I call a CSI system that will help us fight crime and prevent crime. We've recruited a number of people. We've been announced close to 1,100 new jobs in one year, and we're keeping our fingers crossed that we may double that by the end of the year. So very high expectations on what we're doing there. We've created, well, we've tore down silos within planning and development to make certain that entrepreneurs, small businesses, business owners understand what we're doing. We're changing the attitude at the municipal building and the culture that we have a how-to versus a I don't know or a no attitude so we can be very responsive and engage with our customers, which are the citizens of our city. They pay our bills. And when you think about that, we've had a number of different community-engaged task forces. That was a great effort. We were met with challenges, we now see opportunities for growth when we think about the local parks and what we plan to do to reimagine, to revitalize and reinvest into those parks and our entire park system as we focus on quality of life and place initiatives. And the reason why we're focusing on quality of life and place initiatives is because as an elder millennial myself, I understand that we choose where we want to live first before we decide on our career. And as we engage and understand that our brothers and sisters that are aging in place and are age friendly, they too are choosing where they want to reside and retire based on the quality of life. And so we see the nexus between generations that we're all focused on. How do we identify the identity of our city? And we've truly been focused on how our city reestablishes its swagger as the state capital city, that we're charting a culture of being bold, focused on change and overall economic growth for all.
